issue.title: test_scroll_derived_cursor_and_streaming_stays times out waiting for scroll-derived active block b0 under load
issue.description:
`tests/ace/tui/widgets/decks/test_deck_block_spread_pilot.py::test_scroll_derived_cursor_and_streaming_stays` times out at line 238 (`wait_for(... view.active_block_id("reply") == "b0")` after `scroll_to(y=header0)`, 5.0s) under host load (loadavg ~16-18).

Observed by the sase-1b1.8 land agent on 2026-09-27, run serially one test per process:
- master 59f5eff16: 5 failures in 23 runs (also once in a 587-test parallel deck/keymap run).
- pre-sase-1b1.8.2 tree (092fb8bf1): 1 failure in 24 runs.
So it predates the badge-first P work, but the rate may have risen after 80fbe7020 (sase-1b1.8.2 changed SectionTrackingVisual anchor collection in prompt_panel/_section_navigation.py); a worker should check whether the scroll-derived active block waits on an anchor publish that now happens later.

task_type_fields.evidence: master 5/23 fail, pre-8.2 tree 1/24 fail, serial, loadavg 16-18; fails at line 238 wait_for timeout 5s.

issue.creation_reason: Found flaking while the sase-1b1.8 land agent ran the deck suites; it reproduces on the pre-epic tree so it is not landing work.

evidence.note: Relayed by sase-1ex.land from phase sase-1ex.2 (note #1): joined check ToolRun f5a02662134a9f53de0067538eb6ba90 (2026-10-02, tree RSS peak 6.2 GiB, pytest lease 4) failed tests/ace/tui/widgets/decks/test_deck_block_spread_pilot.py::test_scroll_derived_cursor_and_streaming_stays. The test passed in isolation on both the base and patched trees. The mru-snapshot diff touched no deck code.

This workspace's restart-wait launch-blocker change does not touch deck spread code.

Independent reproduction in sase_10 just check ToolRun 95848edc688de198b14a927ab1a120a3 (monitor pytnjnf1hewh, 2026-10-04T21:48:35Z): FAILED tests/ace/tui/widgets/decks/test_deck_block_spread_pilot.py::test_scroll_derived_cursor_and_streaming_stays at line 238, wait_for timed out after 5.0s for view.active_block_id('reply') == 'b0'.
